proposals.before: Crown Prince Zhaoming; Crown Prince Ai; Crown Prince Huai
proposals.after: Crown Prince Zhaoming; Crown Prince Ai; Crown Prince Minhuai
proposals.reason: 愍懷太子 is Minhuai, not truncated Huai; align the third title with the established posthumous name.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month of year three Prince Xing of Shixing died.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month of year three Prince Dan of Shixing died.
proposals.reason: 始興王憺 names Prince of Shixing, personal name Dan (憺); 'Prince Xing' misreads the fief name as a personal name.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month of the third year, Prince Xing of Shixing died.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month of the third year, Prince Dan of Shixing died.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 始興王憺 as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Wu commandery repeatedly lost its harvest to floods; a memorial proposed dredging the Grand Canal to drain the Zhe River.
proposals.after: Wuxing commandery repeatedly lost its harvest to floods; a memorial proposed dredging the Grand Canal to drain the Zhe River.
proposals.reason: 吳興郡 is Wuxing, not Wu; Wu is 吳郡 in the following sentences.

proposals.before: Wu commandery repeatedly because of flood disaster lost harvest; someone memorialized that the Grand Canal should be dredged to drain into the Zhe River.
proposals.after: Wuxing commandery repeatedly because of flood disaster lost harvest; someone memorialized that the Grand Canal should be dredged to drain into the Zhe River.
proposals.reason: 吳興 must be Wuxing, distinct from 吳郡.

proposals.before: In spring of Zhongdatong year two an edict sent former Inspector of Jiaozhi Wang Dan with credentials to levy labor from Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing commanderies.
proposals.after: In spring of Zhongdatong year two an edict sent former Inspector of Jiaozhou Wang Bian with credentials to levy labor from Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing commanderies.
proposals.reason: 王弁 is Wang Bian (弁), not Dan; 交州 is Jiaozhou rather than Jiaozhi in this inspector title.

proposals.before: In spring of the second year of Zhongdatong, an edict sent former Inspector of Jiaozhi Wang Dan with credentials to mobilize civilian labor from the three commanderies Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing for the work.
proposals.after: In spring of the second year of Zhongdatong, an edict sent former Inspector of Jiaozhou Wang Bian with credentials to mobilize civilian labor from the three commanderies Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing for the work.
proposals.reason: Correct 王弁 to Wang Bian and 交州 to Jiaozhou.

proposals.before: The crown prince memorialized: "I hear Wang Dan and others are to levy labor from the three eastern commanderies, open canals, drain Zhen Marsh, and end floods in Wu commandery—truly utmost humane care and far-sighted policy.
proposals.after: The crown prince memorialized: "I hear Wang Bian and others are to levy labor from the three eastern commanderies, open canals, drain Zhen Marsh, and end floods in Wuxing commandery—truly utmost humane care and far-sighted policy.
proposals.reason: Match 王弁 as Wang Bian and 吳興 as Wuxing; the quote is incomplete without the closing, but fix the name/place errors.

proposals.before: I hear Wu commandery has lost harvest year after year and many people have wandered away.
proposals.after: I hear Wuxing commandery has lost harvest year after year and many people have wandered away.

proposals.before: Moreover bandits often watch whether the people are weak or strong; if good men are conscripted, robbery only increases—Wu commandery will not yet gain, while the interior will already suffer.
proposals.after: Moreover bandits often watch whether the people are weak or strong; if good men are conscripted, robbery only increases—Wuxing commandery will not yet gain, while the interior will already suffer.

proposals.before: Emperor Jing at imperial mandate posthumously titled him Crown Prince Minhuai.
proposals.after: Emperor Jing, acting under imperial mandate, posthumously titled him Crown Prince Minhuai.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical: "at imperial mandate" does not correctly render 承制.

decisions.reason: s0002 lists 愍懷太子; the literal truncates 愍懷 to Huai. Crown Prince Minhuai restores the full posthumous title already used elsewhere.
始興王憺 is the Prince of Shixing, personal name Dan (憺). 'Prince Xing' wrongly takes part of the fief name 始興 as a personal name; Prince Dan of Shixing is accurate.
The literal has the same misreading of 始興王憺; replacing Xing with Dan matches the personal name 憺 after the title 始興王.
吳興郡 is Wuxing commandery. Rendering it as Wu conflates it with 吳郡, which s0086 lists separately among the three commanderies.
The literal likewise mistranslates 吳興郡 as Wu; Wuxing is required and distinct from 吳郡 in the following sentence.
前交州刺史王弁 names former Inspector of Jiaozhou Wang Bian (弁). Wang Dan and Jiaozhi invent a wrong given name and substitute 交趾 for the provincial title 交州.
The literal repeats the same errors on 王弁 and 交州; Wang Bian and Jiaozhou match the Chinese office and personal name.
The memorial quotes 王弁 and 吳興一境; correcting Wang Dan to Wang Bian and Wu to Wuxing restores both the person and the place named in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王弁等上東三郡民丁……使吳興一境

decisions.reason: 所聞吳興累年失收 refers to Wuxing; s0091 then turns to 吳郡 separately, so Wu here is a place-name error.
吳興未受其益 names Wuxing as the place that would not yet benefit; Wu again conflates it with 吳郡.
敬帝承制 means Emperor Jing acted under/on imperial mandate; 'at imperial mandate' is ungrammatical and fails to render 承制. The proposed wording is accurate and natural.

claimRetractions.reason: s0086–s0087 have only 王弁 (Wang Bian). The alternate-name claim Wang Dan arises solely from the mistranslation of 弁 as Dan, not from any Chinese variant.
